definitions.definition: DN 22:17-21: as the fifth field of dhamma-contemplation the four truths are known 'as they really are', and each is expanded: suffering as birth, ageing, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, despair, the disliked, the lost, the unobtained, in brief the five aggregates of clinging; origin as threefold craving arising and settling in the dear-looking and pleasant-looking; cessation as the complete fading and ceasing of that craving, in the same places; the way as the noble eightfold path.

name: The noble eightfold path (ariya aṭṭhaṅgika magga)

definitions.definition: DN 22:21: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration, each defined; right mindfulness is defined as the four establishments of mindfulness and right concentration as the four jhānas.
